title: Central Limit Theorems for Outcome Records in Disordered Quantum Trajectories: the second-moment comparison for arbitrary initial states (Proposition 5.4)
author: Lubashan Pathirana
work: Central Limit Theorems for Outcome Records in Disordered Quantum Trajectories
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the paper's second-moment comparison for an arbitrary measurable initial state, printed as Proposition 5.4 (source0.tex lines 4139-4150) and delivered with the paper's own complete proof (lines 4151-4547, 397 lines). The statement is what upgrades the stationary functional central limit theorem to a universal one: under Assumption 1, a dynamically stationary state, the uniform forgetting bound beta_n(eta) <= r_n -> 0 and summable beta_n(vartheta), it shows that the first absolute moment of the partial sums is bounded and that the difference of the second moments under the two annealed outcome laws, divided by n, vanishes. The proof is a paper-specific comparison of the coupled posterior states: it writes the difference Phi^{(i-1)}_omega(vartheta(omega)) - rho_ss(theta^{i-1} omega) of the two starting states, expands the partial sums of the centered observable against both annealed laws, controls the resulting cross terms through the per-step forgetting bounds beta_i, sums the resulting majorants using the summability of (beta_n(vartheta)) and the uniform bound r_n -> 0, and concludes that any stationary second-moment limit is also the second-moment and covariance limit under the arbitrary initial law. This is not a qualifying-examination exercise: it is a source-local estimate that has to be assembled from the coupling of two different quantum trajectory laws, the trace-norm forgetting of the non-selective channel cocycle and the block structure of the outcome records, and it is one of the two propositions on which the paper's universal CLT rests. The unit is therefore H2.
